editions.body_excerpt:
View this post on the web at https://www.latent.space/p/ainews-glm-52-the-top-frontend-coding

Last 6 days before regular tickets sell out at AI Engineer World’s Fair [ https://substack.com/redirect/5b9ca9ae-df72-43da-8bd6-b722048499d2?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] - this is the single biggest gathering of AI Engineers, Founders, Leaders, and Researchers in the world. Talk tracks are looking FANTASTIC. Join us.
Since February [ https://substack.com/redirect/9953f26d-1755-4b0d-ad10-0e853b8aa874?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] we have been banging the drum about GLM 5, Z.ai’s biggest model launch that nudged it ahead of top open model labs like DeepSeek, Mistral, Cohere and Moonshot in most evals. 5.1 was more of a minor update, but 5.2, released opportunistically this weekend [ https://substack.com/redirect/d2f500bd-0939-40d4-b01b-fdc82dead959?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] after the Fable ban [ https://substack.com/redirect/1dcaaf82-96e5-4527-af95-d0f836b46f54?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] (still unresolved [ https://substack.com/redirect/8db7e559-0ce9-4c60-8456-d8c91ee1e5da?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]), is a much stronger play at being your default coding model:
This third party eval validates official offline evals [ https://substack.com/redirect/b5ff7939-3fa8-40d9-923b-67ed795eb1d7?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] that put GLM 5.2 just behind Opus 4.8 as the best coding model in the world - an impressive feat for a merely 744B parameter model (vs Opus rumored to be at least twice as large [ https://substack.com/redirect/2e2919a4-9230-4b35-93fa-bbc23a573aae?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], with Cursor’s next Composer model also in that range). But it is a particularly notable achievement to beat ALL Opuses, including 4.8, at frontend coding [ https://substack.com/redirect/957e8289-6191-45b7-9568-5d1e83a5fa51?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], a key battleground:
 
Technical disclosures are light - no paper, just a minor improvement on DeepSeek Sparse Attention that improves efficiency at ultra long contexts:
AI News for 6/15/2026-6/16/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters [ https://substack.com/redirect/c5a74f47-da8d-4599-abd3-4d0cbcf41ae9?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] and no further Discords. AINews’ website [ https://substack.com/redirect/626109a6-d796-4e09-9a2e-82425b654ffe?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space [ https://substack.com/redirect/5149c7d1-16c3-4361-b0a3-5c85e438b17e?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]. You can opt in/out [ https://substack.com/redirect/326121b9-ab52-4203-a33b-81f8c243e6a8?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] of email frequencies!
AI Twitter Recap
Top Story: GLM 5.2 release and technical details
What happened
Z.ai released GLM-5.2 as an MIT-licensed open-weight frontier model aimed at coding and long-horizon agentic work.
Z.ai announced GLM-5.2 [ https://substack.com/redirect/1eb4624f-6422-441d-8afd-6f4ef53924dc?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], emphasizing coding/agentic improvements, a 1M-token context window, two reasoning-effort modes (high and max), and same API pricing as GLM-5.1.
Z.ai separately highlighted that the release includes infrastructure innovations for 1M context and agentic RL in the technical blog, not just benchmark claims @Zai_org [ https://substack.com/redirect/fd23612d-4edd-4cfd-827b-2d470a9139f6?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ].
The model was immediately positioned by third parties as the strongest open-weight coding/agent model yet, with notable independent leaderboard placements on FrontierSWE per @ProximalHQ [ https://substack.com/redirect/f10df6a9-6884-4339-82f4-2e1a6af8bbb2?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], Design Arena per @Designarena [ https://substack.com/redirect/e63b604e-3350-4199-b0e3-b0e3cb4300f2?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], Agent Arena per @arena [ https://substack.com/redirect/0d639fb9-3a89-4f9f-b42d-0fdcce3e39de?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], and Code Arena: Frontend per @arena [ https://substack.com/redirect/f3a9b2c3-731b-44b6-968d-1252d40ee86d?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ].
Ecosystem support landed on day 0 across inference stacks and platforms including Transformers/vLLM/SGLang noted by @mervenoyann [ https://substack.com/redirect/8e0608f0-3a62-4529-88e9-f676f97757fe?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], SGLang [ https://substack.com/redirect/194bb35a-5ad5-4b98-bda4-8469ec7f3329?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], vLLM [ https://substack.com/redirect/0044f5a8-afa0-449e-b707-f65aa6e85f9d?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], Cloudflare Workers AI [ https://substack.com/redirect/7fd2921f-91da-459b-ba13-badd22d5b45e?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], OpenRouter [ https://substack.com/redirect/6c2a24aa-e51c-4d69-b7e1-59d63319c4aa?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], Ollama Cloud [ https://substack.com/redirect/d13a4921-4518-4b13-b198-ef5a95dcf465?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], Baseten [ https://substack.com/redirect/66a8a533-ffde-47b9-ac69-ff393777cdfe?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], DeepInfra [ https://substack.com/redirect/82b8f0ff-0e6a-4a91-ba46-380b079bf7e9?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], Fireworks [ https://substack.com/redirect/6371a2fe-fc9e-46cb-b55b-990ad9327f0a?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], Notion [ https://substack.com/redirect/42558957-d7c1-431a-977b-199724596946?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], and others.
Commentary from practitioners who tested early access was unusually strong, with @Sentdex [ https://substack.com/redirect/af9349f3-50e6-49cd-b162-2eefb9bf0f8e?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] calling it the first open model he could plausibly substitute for Opus/GPT-class workflows, while more skeptical voices asked for additional evals and long-horizon validation @scaling01 [ https://substack.com/redirect/568a6a1a-68bf-4cb6-8dec-b90997a9752e?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], @omarsar0 [ https://substack.com/redirect/9d881493-0299-4702-a535-9f6a3766b4cb?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], @teortaxesTex [ https://substack.com/redirect/401214db-e80c-4fc0-ac72-96bd0021a994?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ].
Core facts
Official release claims
From Z.ai’s release posts and downstream launch-partner summaries:
License: MIT open weights @Zai_org [ https://substack.com/redirect/1eb4624f-6422-441d-8afd-6f4ef53924dc?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]
Primary target: coding, agentic tasks, long-horizon execution @Zai_org [ https://substack.com/redirect/1eb4624f-6422-441d-8afd-6f4ef53924dc?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]
Context window: 1M tokens @Zai_org [ https://substack.com/redirect/1eb4624f-6422-441d-8afd-6f4ef53924dc?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]
Reasoning modes: GLM-5.2 (max) and GLM-5.2 (high) @Zai_org [ https://substack.com/redirect/1eb4624f-6422-441d-8afd-6f4ef53924dc?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]
API pricing: same as GLM-5.1; Agent Arena gives explicit pricing of $1.4 / $4.4 per input/output MTokens @arena [ https://substack.com/redirect/0d639fb9-3a89-4f9f-b42d-0fdcce3e39de?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]
Architecture: launch partners repeatedly describe it as a 744B-parameter MoE with 40B active parameters per token @friendliai [ https://substack.com/redirect/6200ceb6-6c19-475a-a852-c47ee58cd892?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], @DeepInfra [ https://substack.com/redirect/82b8f0ff-0e6a-4a91-ba46-380b079bf7e9?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]
Attention/inference design: built on DeepSeek Sparse Attention, extended with IndexShare @friendliai [ https://substack.com/redirect/6200ceb6-6c19-475a-a852-c47ee58cd892?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], @lmsysorg [ https://substack.com/redirect/194bb35a-5ad5-4b98-bda4-8469ec7f3329?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]
Speculative decoding support: improved MTP (multi-token prediction) to boost acceptance rate @mervenoyann [ https://substack.com/redirect/8e0608f0-3a62-4529-88e9-f676f97757fe?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], @lmsysorg [ https://substack.com/redirect/194bb35a-5ad5-4b98-bda4-8469ec7f3329?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]
Independent benchmark/leaderboard points cited in tweets
FrontierSWE: ranked #3 overall, behind Fable 5 and Opus 4.8, and ahead of GPT-5.5 according to @ProximalHQ [ https://substack.com/redirect/f10df6a9-6884-4339-82f4-2e1a6af8bbb2?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]
Design Arena: #1, Elo 1360, +27 Elo and +4 positions, passing the unavailable Claude Fable 5 per @Designarena [ https://substack.com/redirect/e63b604e-3350-4199-b0e3-b0e3cb4300f2?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]
Agent Arena: GLM-5.2 (Max) ranked #10 overall, #1 open model by a wide margin, up from #13; same post notes a steerability tradeoff @arena [ https://substack.com/redirect/0d639fb9-3a89-4f9f-b42d-0fdcce3e39de?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]
Code Arena: Frontend: GLM-5.2 (Max) ranked #2 overall, +29 points over Claude Opus 4.7 (Thinking), behind only Fable 5; #2 React, #4 HTML @arena [ https://substack.com/redirect/f3a9b2c3-731b-44b6-968d-1252d40ee86d?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]
Text Arena: only #25 overall, roughly similar to GLM-5.1, though with gains in Expert Arena, Multi-Turn, and occupations including Medicine & Healthcare @arena [ https://substack.com/redirect/de47312d-808a-4eff-a8ce-844364f086d8?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]
Terminal-Bench 2.1: 81.0 for GLM-5.2 vs 62.0 for GLM-5.1 per @lmsysorg [ https://substack.com/redirect/194bb35a-5ad5-4b98-bda4-8469ec7f3329?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]
Additional benchmark claims aggregated by @TheRundownAI [ https://substack.com/redirect/570fcd91-0dc5-4799-942a-197bdd59e9aa?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]:
74.4 on long-horizon coding, ahead of GPT-5.5’s 72.6
62.1 on SWE-bench Pro, ahead of GPT-5.5
99.2 on AIME 2026, ahead of Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5
Multiple users highlighted it as the first open-weight model to cross 80% on Terminal-Bench @cline [ https://substack.com/redirect/724b827e-4dd0-457a-a642-13086e0d6011?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]

editions.subject: ☕️ Nvidia joins the AI debt boom
editions.body_excerpt: ☕️ SpaceX acquires AI startup for $60B SpaceX's $60B Cursor deal, OpenAI's exploding losses, and more. Read online Tuesday 16 June 2026 | Join Free | UpgradeTogether withHi there, this is your daily ☕️ Techpresso.In today's newsletter:🚀 SpaceX acquires Cursor for $60B💸 OpenAI's losses just exploded nearly 8X🤖 Facebook's new AI knows more about you than you think💰 Nvidia joins the AI debt boom🚫 Chrome is closing the last loophole for ad blockers🧵 Threads just hit half a billion usersPlus: 🎁 12 other news you might like, 🧰 6 tools, and 📚 4 papers.FROM OUR PARTNERWhat are the risks leaders don’t see?Executives plan for risk. What's harder to manage are the ones you can't see—lagging insight, hidden misalignment, systems that fail under pressure. These blind spots are where AI strategies stall.The C-suite that surfaces them first moves faster:Close gaps in real-time visibilityAlign teams before scaling breaksBuild systems that hold under pressureRead more in C-Suite Takeaways ‘Where executive decisions meet real-time pressure' 🚀 SpaceX acquires Cursor for $60B LINKSpaceX is buying Anysphere, the company behind the AI coding assistant Cursor, in an all-stock deal worth $60 billion, pushing Elon Musk's company well beyond rockets, satellites, and AI models into developer software.According to a Form 8-K filed with the SEC on June 16, Cursor shareholders will get SpaceX Class A common stock, and the transaction is expected to close in the third quarter of 2026, pending regulatory approval.Cursor has passed 1 million paying customers and more than $2 billion in annualized revenue, with revenue projected to reach $6 billion by the end of 2026, meaning SpaceX is paying roughly 20 to 30 times current revenue. 💸 OpenAI's losses just exploded nearly 8X LINKOpenAI's net loss attributable to the company jumped from $5.09 billion in 2024 to $38.53 billion in 2025, according to audited financial documents independently verified by the Financial Times.In 2025, OpenAI had $13.07 billion in revenue against $34 billion in total costs and expenses, including $19.18 billion on research and development, leaving a $20.92 billion loss from operations.Converting from a non-profit to a for-profit triggered a $41.55 billion loss from changes in fair value, pushing the net loss to $60.35 billion before $21.82 billion was removed via noncontrolling interests. 🤖 Facebook's new AI knows more about you than you think LINKFacebook is rolling out "AI Mode," a new way to search the platform using Meta AI, which pulls answers from public posts across Facebook, including Groups and Reels, instead of showing a list of results.Rather than scrolling through search results, users can ask a question in plain language and get a synthesized answer based on what people are actively discussing across the platform.Because the AI summarizes content from everyday users instead of vetted sources, there's a real risk of outdated or misleading information slipping through, a concern already raised about Google's own AI Mode on Reddit. 💰 Nvidia joins the AI debt boom LINKNvidia is raising at least $20 billion through bonds, its first such sale since 2021, joining other tech companies that have taken on debt to fund the AI buildout, Bloomberg reports.The chipmaker is offering the bonds in seven tranches with maturities running from two to 30 years, and the longest tranche carries a spread of about 0.9 percentage points above U.S. Treasuries.Nvidia plans to use the money for general corporate purposes, including refinancing existing debt, with JPMorgan Chase, Morgan Stanley, and Goldman Sachs among the banks managing the sale. 🚫 Chrome is closing the last loophole for ad blockers LINKGoogle is ending support for Manifest V2 extensions in Chrome versions 150 and 151, a move that will break many popular ad blockers built on that older technology over the next couple of releases.Under Manifest V3, extensions can no longer intercept data dynamically, so the new compliant ad blockers on the Chrome Web Store rely on predefined lists to work, making them less effective than before.People who want to avoid Chrome's strict Manifest V3 rules can switch to Mozilla's Firefox, which supports both Manifest V2 and V3 at the same time, or try a VPN with ad-blocking services like NordVPN. 🧵 Threads just hit half a billion users LINKMeta's Threads app has passed half a billion users, hitting 500 million monthly users this month and adding about 100 million new users since last August, with the company crediting its "communities" feature for the recent growth.Meta claims growth is now more organic as more people open Threads directly instead of clicking through Instagram or Facebook, and it pointed to gains in Asia, where time spent rose 80 percent in South Korea and 130 percent in Japan.Meta hasn't shared daily active users since October, when Threads reached 150 million, and the app still doesn't drive revenue, with CFO Susan Li saying in April it won't be a "meaningful driver" of revenue growth in 2026.FROM OUR PARTNERCreators Are All In on Creative AI — On Their Own TermsAdobe's latest Creators' Toolkit Report surveyed 16,000+ creators globally.The findings are clear:87% say creative AI is growing their business and audience75% describe it as integrated or essential to their workflow85% say the final creative decision should stay theirsCreative AI is fueling the creator economy. But the creators who stand out use it to amplify their POV, not just create more content.Learn more on Adobe's newsroom.  MiniMax opens model weights to the public
 




 6,523 Likes
 



 







The weights for MiniMax M3 just dropped on Hugging Face. Here is what you need to know.M3 is the first open-weight model to combine frontier coding, a 1 million token context window, and native multimodal support (images and video) in one package. That combo was locked behind paid APIs until now.The 1M context window is the big deal. A new sparse attention design drops the compute cost at 1M context to roughly 1/20th of the previous generation, so it does not cost a fortune to run long contexts.On the coding side: M3 scores 59.0% on SWE-Bench Pro, ahead of GPT-5.5 at 58.6%.Feed it an entire codebase at once, no chunking neededSend images and video directly, no separate vision modelControl a desktop computer, similar to Anthropic's computer-use APIToggle a thinking mode on or off per requestAPI pricing starts at $0.30 per million input tokens. Weights are now on Hugging Face to self-host.

 Nex catches Rio 3.5 secretly built on their open-source model without credit
 




 5,338 Likes
 



 







A city government in Rio de Janeiro released a model called Rio 3.5, claimed it was original, and the AI world went nuts. Then Nex AGI did the math.Turns out Rio 3.5 is just a weight merge (think: blending two existing models together like mixing paint) of two open-source models: 60% Nex N2 Pro + 40% Qwen 3.5. No original training. No novel research. Just a blend with a new name.The smoking gun? Strip away Rio's system prompt and the model literally introduces itself as Nex N2 Pro.Here is what you actually get with the real Nex N2 Pro:Free, Apache 2.0 license, weights on Hugging Face75.3 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, top-3 globally, beating Claude Opus 4.7Adaptive Thinking: the model decides how deeply to reason per task, cutting wasted compute by up to 50%Run it free today via OpenRouter or deploy locally with their sglang forkThe takeaway: open-source attribution matters. And the real model was free the whole time.
